narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **41% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this isn’t a certainty, it’s high enough that your school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign—your current path has some risks, and these courses are a way to give you the support you need to stay on track.

The biggest reason behind this recommendation is that the model noticed **you don’t plan to pursue higher education after finishing school**. Most students who *do* aim for further studies tend to work harder and stay more engaged, which helps them avoid struggles later. Since you haven’t expressed that goal, the model sees this as a signal that you might not be putting in the effort needed to pass your final exams.

Another key factor is that **you haven’t had any past class failures**, which is actually a positive sign—most students who struggle later often have a history of failing subjects earlier. But because you haven’t faced those challenges before, the model is concerned that you might not be fully prepared for the demands of your final year.

Finally, the model also picked up on **who your guardian is**. While this isn’t about judgment, research shows that students with mothers as guardians often have more support at home, which can make a big difference in academic success. Since your guardian is your father, the model is gently flagging that you might benefit from extra guidance to ensure you don’t fall behind.

This doesn’t mean you *will* fail—it means your school wants to give you a safety net. The remedial courses are designed to help you fill any gaps before they become problems. Instead of seeing this as a punishment, think of it as a chance to get ahead. Talk to your teachers about where you might need extra help, and use this opportunity to strengthen your study habits. With the right focus, you can turn this into a stepping stone for success.
